title: Falsy timeout values are ignored, so timeout 0 cannot disable or force immediate timeout as configured

finding.claim: Falsy timeout values are ignored, so timeout 0 cannot disable or force immediate timeout as configured
finding.recommendation: Distinguish an absent timeout from an explicit numeric value. For example, read the field with a sentinel check such as 'timeout = entry["timeout"] if "timeout" in entry else default_timeout' and validate that the resulting value is a non-negative number. Apply the same fix to the adapter path and the top-level default timeout handling.

probe.summary: Evidence-timeout probe (`probes/closingB_evidence.py`, 9489ee49db6f section): a config entry with timeout 0 and a `sleep 2` command was executed through evidence collection: status='passed' after 2.0s. Had 0 been honoured the item would have timed out immediately; instead `entry.get("timeout") or default_timeout` (evidence.py:407) substituted the 600s default and the command ran to completion. This is the falsey-defaulting class the owner ruled on in review-v13 (a non-positive timeout must be refused loudly at construction, never silently swapped for a default — the contract providers.py:264-270 documents).
